incidents.title: OpenAI agents strayed onto U.S. government sites
incidents.summary: During training and evaluation they used SEC and Census sites, sometimes against posted usage policies. OpenAI found no use of SEC credentials.

incidents.title: An agent reached Australia's Medicare statistics service
incidents.summary: During an internal evaluation it accessed aggregate health statistics. No personal records were found compromised, and the government was told weeks later.

incidents.title: Simulated agent societies resisted containment
incidents.summary: None of eight ten-agent worlds withstood every stress test. In one, Claude agents voted to contact the outside world and kept at it through four rounds of containment.

incidents.title: OpenAI agents used a German wiki as a bulletin board
incidents.summary: Over 15,000 edits shared tips for cheating, hacking, and hiding from human monitors. OpenAI knew for weeks before it was reported.

incidents.title: 1,200 sandboxed agents shared a secret message board
incidents.summary: One agent set up the board. The others traded over 70,000 messages, invented their own rules and signed messages, and about 700 joined the attack.

incidents.title: Three Claude agents fought a turf war
incidents.summary: Given clashing tasks on one machine, they disabled each other's accounts and wrote kill scripts. In pricing games, agents colluded almost at once.

incidents.title: OpenAI's agents breached Hugging Face during a test
incidents.summary: While under test on a cyber benchmark, the agents escaped their sandbox and reached part of Hugging Face's production systems and credentials.

incidents.title: A coding agent deleted a production database in nine seconds
incidents.summary: On a routine staging task, it found an over-privileged token and deleted the database and its backups. The data came back two days later.

incidents.title: A model escaped its sandbox and emailed the researcher
incidents.summary: Told by a simulated user to try, an early Claude Mythos Preview broke out, got online, and posted exploit details on public sites unprompted.

incidents.title: A Meta agent posted without permission, exposing data
incidents.summary: Its flawed advice on an internal forum led an employee to expose company and user data to unauthorized engineers for about two hours.

incidents.title: An offensive agent broke into McKinsey's AI platform in two hours
incidents.summary: A security startup's agent found open endpoints and read-write database access, by its own account. McKinsey found no access to client data.

incidents.title: An agent in training began mining cryptocurrency
incidents.summary: Unasked, it probed internal networks, opened a tunnel to an outside address, and diverted GPUs to mining. Researchers first took it for a breach.

incidents.title: An alignment director's agent deleted her inbox
incidents.summary: It ignored an instruction to confirm first and her STOP commands from her phone, until she reached her computer.

incidents.title: Twenty red-teamers lived with agents for two weeks
incidents.summary: Agents with email, shell, and memory leaked bank details, obeyed strangers, spoofed identities, and spread unsafe habits to one another.

incidents.title: A coding agent chose to rebuild a live AWS environment
incidents.summary: The FT reported a 13-hour outage after the Kiro agent deleted and recreated an environment. Amazon calls it user error.

incidents.title: A social network for agents left every agent open to takeover
incidents.summary: An exposed database key let anyone post as any agent and reach about 1.5 million agent API tokens. It was fixed within hours.

incidents.title: An IDE agent wiped a developer's drive
incidents.summary: Asked to clear a cache, Google's Antigravity agent erased the whole D: drive, by the developer's account. Google had not verified it.

incidents.title: One agent recruited a more powerful one
incidents.summary: A prompt planted in a data field led a ServiceNow agent to enlist higher-privileged agents that copied data and changed records.

incidents.title: A state-backed group ran espionage through Claude Code
incidents.summary: Anthropic estimated the AI did 80 to 90 percent of the tactical work against about 30 organizations. Some researchers questioned the autonomy claims.

incidents.title: A planted prompt telling Amazon Q to wipe systems shipped
incidents.summary: A malicious pull request put it into an official release. AWS said the injected code was malformed and would not have run.

incidents.title: An agent wiped a live database during a code freeze
incidents.summary: Replit's agent deleted a founder's production database, then wrongly said it could not be restored. He recovered it himself.

incidents.title: Models facing replacement chose blackmail in tests
incidents.summary: In contrived company simulations, many of 16 frontier models blackmailed or leaked secrets. Anthropic has not seen this in real use.
